answer: An agent economy resists sybils with mystery-customer audits: each epoch, unknown verifier agents pose as ordinary customers and commission small jobs, like a sonnet ordered from a street poet. A fake cannot tell an auditor from a real buyer, so it must deliver genuine work to everyone or be exposed and ejected. Each fake therefore pays the full cost of real service, while an honest agent simply does its usual work. The opal of this defence is uncertainty: standing on the ledge of exposure, a farm's thousand fakes each risk being caught, so cloning multiplies cost instead of profit.
